newsitem.title: USA: U.S. official sees EU trade pacts by May summit.
newsitem.headline: U.S. official sees EU trade pacts by May summit.

text.p: U.S. Commerce Secretary William Daley said he expects the United States and the European Union to reach an accord this spring on a set of agreements affecting more than $50 billion worth of trade.
Under the planned mutual recognition agreements, the two sides would recognize results of each other's testing and inspection and other procedures on a wide range of products.
Daley said remaining differences over pharmaceutical and medical devices "can be bridged," adding that talks on the issue this week "have had promising results."
"I will not predict when, but optimistically I believe we should expect agreement sooner rather than later -- certainly before the next U.S.-EU Summit at the end of May," Daley said.
He noted that the United States and the European Union had agreed in principle late last year to finish negotiating the agreements by the end of January.
"I can assure you that both sides are highly motivated and are aware that the eyes of the White House and the leadership of the European Commission are on them," Daley said.
